articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski’s 7-Year Quest for the Lightweight Title
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has chased a second UFC belt for seven years. This is the full story of Volk’s quest to become a two-division champion, from his featherweight title win over Max Holloway to two fights with Islam Makhachev, the Ilia Topuria knockout, and his call for a lightweight super fight with Justin Gaethje after UFC 333. Before the belts, Volkanovski was a concreter from Wollongong, Australia, who played rugby league at as much as 214 pounds. He cut down to featherweight, went unbeaten in the UFC on the way to a title shot, and started looking up at lightweight in 2021. He lost to Makhachev twice in 2023, lost his featherweight title to Topuria in 2024, then came back to beat Diego Lopes twice and finish the undefeated Movsar Evloev. Now, he says, a fight with Gaethje is “something I would retire for.” Told in Volk’s own words, with Dana White, from MMA Weekly’s press conferences, media days and weigh-ins, 2019 to 2026. Should the UFC give Volkanovski his shot at the lightweight title? Tell us in the comments. articles.title: I feel like Chimaev agreed with me #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen thought Khamzat Chimaev might be reaching for a weapon. Turns out, it was nothing like that. Chael tells a hilarious story about an encounter with Khamzat, who at the time didn't have a beard. Chael tells him to stop, and Khamzat immediately pulls up his pant leg and starts reaching toward his sock. For a moment, Chael doesn't know what he's about to pull out. Is it a holster? A knife? Something else? But the explanation is much simpler—and a lot funnier. Khamzat was wearing a slip-on Vans shoe that had come off, and he was just trying to get his foot back inside. Even Chael has to laugh at the misunderstanding. He says Khamzat seemed to understand why he told him to stop. A funny behind-the-scenes Khamzat Chimaev story from Chael Sonnen. #ChaelSonnen #KhamzatChimaev #UFC #MMA #UFCStories #MMAStories

articles.title: Jake Paul has a date and location but no opponent
articles.description: Jake Paul has a date. He has a location. What he apparently doesn't have yet is an opponent. Chael Sonnen doesn't believe Jake can necessarily go wrong with the choice, but the list of possibilities is getting interesting. Francis Ngannou remains a possibility after Jake previously called him out. Nate Diaz is expected to participate on the Abu Dhabi card, although Chael doesn't believe that necessarily means he'll face Jake. Mike Perry could also be involved, but Jake has already competed against both men. Then there are the elite boxers. Chael doesn't expect Jake to go that direction either. So who's left? If Jake's opponent were already locked in, Chael believes we probably would have heard the name with the announcement. That means the search may still be happening and the reaction from the fans could matter. Jake Paul is fighting in Abu Dhabi on Christmas Eve. Who do you want standing across from him? #JakePaul #Boxing #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Money Moicano Made a BIG Mistake
articles.description: Renato Moicano says he wants to fight out his UFC contract. Chael Sonnen thinks saying that publicly was a mistake. If your goal is to reach the end of your contract, the first rule should be simple: don't tell the promoter that's what you're planning to do. Moicano has built himself into one of MMA's most interesting personalities. He's headlining this weekend, getting the press conference spotlight, and the UFC keeps investing promotional resources in him because people want to hear what he has to say. But now he's 37, he's an underdog against Tom Nolan, and he's publicly announced that he intends to fight out his deal. That changes the equation. Why would the UFC continue giving Moicano main events and promotional opportunities if it believes he's preparing to leave? Talking helped Moicano get here. Chael just hopes talking doesn't cost him the very opportunities he worked so hard to earn. #RenatoMoicano #MoneyMoicano #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Volkanovski Finally Had a GOOD Idea
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski finally came up with an idea Chael Sonnen loves. Vacate the featherweight championship. Move to 155 pounds. And fight Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski originally called out Justin Gaethje, but there was a problem: that fight would effectively take away the opportunity Arman had already earned. Now Volk has changed the proposal. If Gaethje walks away from the sport and the lightweight championship becomes vacant, Volkanovski wants Arman. Chael loves it. Volk gets the challenge he says he wants. Arman gets the championship opportunity he earned. And featherweight can move forward with contenders like Aljamain Sterling and Jean Silva competing for the vacant belt. There may also be something else behind Volk's announcement. Chael believes Volkanovski is hearing the same whispers around the sport that everyone else is starting to hear: Justin Gaethje may be much closer to retirement than 50-50. Whatever prompted it, Chael is sold. Volkanovski vs. Tsarukyan is the best idea Volk has offered yet. #AlexanderVolkanovski #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There Is NO Debate: O'Malley vs. Yan Is Next
articles.description: Sean O'Malley says there is no debate and no argument: the Petr Yan rematch is next. Chael Sonnen agrees. What makes O'Malley's statement so powerful is that he almost never does this. Throughout his rise, Sean accepted fights that Chael didn't always understand, went out and did his job, and rarely demanded a specific opponent. Now he's finally playing that card. Petr Yan has every right to take his time after reclaiming the championship, but Chael believes Yan will eventually say yes. He's a competitor first, and a rematch with O'Malley gives him exactly the kind of challenge that has defined his career. If O'Malley can get Yan to publicly agree, the UFC has a very easy decision to make. They have history. They have unfinished business. And now O'Malley has finally spoken up. There is no debate. There is no argument. O'Malley vs. Yan 2 is next. #SeanOMalley #PetrYan #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There’s Nobody for Khamzat Chimaev to Fight
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael He has separated himself from the rest of the middleweight division. After what he did to Robert Whittaker and Dricus Du Plessis, I don’t think you can responsibly throw him in there with the No. 8 or No. 9 guy just to keep him busy. Khamzat is that good. So does he wait? Normally, I hate that idea. But with Sean Strickland and Nassourdine Imavov matched up, I’m not sure there’s a better option. Khamzat told us himself: call me soon, or don’t call me for a while. He wanted time to heal if the UFC didn’t need him right away. For once, waiting might actually make sense. Let Strickland and Imavov settle it, then put Khamzat in there with the winner. He’s clearly next. articles.title: What is Volkanovski thinking? #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen thinks Alexander Volkanovski has come up with one of the dumbest ideas he’s ever heard. Volkanovski’s idea of moving to 155 pounds to test himself raises one big question for Chael: what does a fight with Justin Gaethje actually accomplish? Chael doesn’t see who benefits from that matchup, especially when Volkanovski could make a much bigger statement by fully committing to the lightweight division. If Volk really wants to test himself, Chael argues, he should be willing to drop the belt and go all in. He points to Ilia Topuria as the example of a fighter willing to make a major move rather than simply talk about taking on a new challenge. Chael makes his position clear: being a great fighter doesn’t require being a great promoter. If Volkanovski wants to prove himself at lightweight, Chael believes he needs to make the commitment. Is Volk’s idea a smart move—or does Chael have a point? Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen analysis, UFC news, and MMA breakdowns. #ChaelSonnen #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA

articles.title: Reyes Owes Daniel Cormier an Apology #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen believes Dominick Reyes owes Daniel Cormier an apology. But what did DC actually say, and was Reyes justified in accusing him of bias? Chael breaks down the controversy surrounding Cormier’s comments about Reyes and fighters from the Caucasus region. In Chael’s view, Daniel wasn’t putting Reyes down or giving him an unfair shake. He was simply acknowledging what he saw: Reyes looked really good. Chael also explains why Cormier referring to Reyes as a “kid” shouldn’t automatically be interpreted as disrespect. Drawing from his own experience with Jon Jones, Chael argues that the context matters—and that Reyes may have been given the wrong impression about what Daniel meant. Ultimately, Chael says he wants to defend Reyes, but he can’t make the case. He believes Daniel Cormier’s hands were clean and that Reyes got this one wrong. Was DC being unfair, or did Reyes misread the situation? articles.title: Sean Strickland Finally Came to His Senses…
articles.description: Sean Strickland finally came to his senses. After questioning whether he wanted to keep competing, Strickland has agreed to face Nassourdine Imavov in February. And Chael Sonnen believes he made the right choice. This was the opponent Sean originally stood up for. When the UFC was looking at a Khamzat Chimaev rematch, Strickland said Imavov deserved the first opportunity. Then Sean had his motorcycle accident, started questioning what he wanted to do, and the entire situation changed. Now he's back. Chael doesn't know what changed between December and February. The opponent is the same. The championship is the same. The only thing that appears to have changed is Sean. Whatever the reason, Chael believes Strickland made the right decision. He's the champion, Imavov earned the opportunity, and now they're going to settle it. Everything is right again. #SeanStrickland #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There Is NO ONE I Want to See Volkanovski Fight…
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has a problem: there is nobody I want to see him fight. He’s throwing out Aljamain Sterling at 145, Justin Gaethje at 155, and now Ilia Topuria. When the champion has three different ideas across two divisions, that tells me he doesn’t actually have a fight. Volk says he wants to challenge himself. Fine. Of the three ideas he gave us, there’s one I’ll support: drop the featherweight belt, move to 155 and fight Ilia. You lost to Ilia. You want that one back. You’re both at 155 now. On behalf of the community, we accept. Drop the belt. Go to lightweight. Fight Ilia. articles.title: Did the Judges Get Merab vs. Yan Wrong? #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen was stunned when Petr Yan was awarded the victory over Merab Dvalishvili. Chael explains why he thought Merab won the first three rounds, pointing to the relentless pressure, forward movement, and pace that defined Merab's performance. In Chael's view, Merab continued to push the action through the opening rounds. But one moment stood out: Yan landed a body shot in the third that visibly affected Merab. Merab flinched before smiling, and Chael acknowledges that it was an excellent shot. Even so, he still believed Merab had done enough to win the round. Was that body shot enough to change the round, or did Merab's pressure and activity deserve more credit on the scorecards? Chael breaks down the fight and explains why the decision surprised him. articles.title: Is Islam Makhachev Still the Undisputed Champion? #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed UFC champion if an interim champion is crowned? Chael Sonnen raises a question about the UFC's championship system: can a title truly be undisputed when another fighter holds an interim belt in the same division? Chael makes an important distinction. He isn't saying Islam has lost his championship. He's arguing that Islam's status as the *undisputed* champion is now open to debate, because the winner of the interim title fight between Morales and Prates would have a competing claim. Chael also questions why an interim title is being introduced when the situation doesn't appear to involve the usual circumstance of a champion being sidelined by injury. Is this just a matter of terminology, or does an interim belt fundamentally change the meaning of being undisputed? Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen analysis, UFC championship debates, MMA news, and fight breakdowns. #IslamMakhachev #UFC #ChaelSonnen #InterimChampion #MMA #UFCNews

articles.title: Alex Pereira Is NOT a Small Heavyweight
articles.description: Alex Pereira says if heavyweight doesn’t work out, he can go back to 205 because he’s “not a big heavyweight.” I was so surprised by that statement that I questioned whether Pereira had actually said it. My editing team had to send me the proof. Israel Adesanya didn’t like it either. His point was simple: Pereira shouldn’t be making excuses after the Ciryl Gane fight or before he steps in there with Sergei Pavlovich. But there’s another problem—I don’t buy that Pereira is a small heavyweight. He’s taller than most heavyweight champions, has a longer reach than almost all of them and weighs around 240 pounds. If Pereira wins the heavyweight championship, we’ll suddenly be having a very different conversation about where he belongs in the all-time discussion. articles.title: I Was in the Middle of the Arman Tsarukyan–Dillon Danis Brawl
articles.description: RAF 14 had a little bit of everything. Dillon Danis was on fire at the press conference before things got out of control with Arman Tsarukyan and Khamzat Chimaev. What happened afterward impressed me even more. Dillon still had nearly nine pounds to cut, security had been doubled, and there were plenty of reasons he could have walked away. He didn’t. He made the weight and showed up. Jordan Burroughs once again showed why what he’s doing at this stage of his career separates him from the other names in the GOAT conversation. Vito Arujau and Sebastian Rivera produced an incredible comeback, and Jordan Oliver once again refused to pass the torch. articles.description: Dana White called Alexander Volkanovski “an absolute stud” after he finished previously unbeaten Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 post-fight press conference, and said “this guy’s built different.” Asked if the UFC would let Volk move up to lightweight to fight Justin Gaethje, Dana basically gave him the green light: “When you’ve accomplished what he’s accomplished, there’s not much we’re gonna say no to with him.” Should Volkanovski go up and fight Gaethje? articles.title: Dana White on Islam Makhachev: "You Can't Hold Up Divisions Like This"
articles.description: Dana on Islam: "You Can't Hold Up Divisions Like This" Asked why Toronto is getting an interim title fight at the UFC 333 post-fight press conference, Dana White didn't dance around it: Islam Makhachev averages about one fight a year, was slated for January, then said he didn't want to fight until after Ramadan. Dana says he gave no reason and simply changed his mind after saying he'd fight before Ramadan — so the division kept moving without him. Was Dana right to move on without Islam Makhachev?
